title: The Eval-Reproducibility Link: Can an Outsider Reproduce Any Published Dangerous-Capability Claim?

original_idea.body:
# The Eval-Reproducibility Link: Can an Outsider Reproduce Any Published Dangerous-Capability Claim?

**Problem:** Trust-in-evals chain: 'lab runs dangerous-capability eval' -> 'reports a result' -> 'third party can reproduce' -> 'claim is trustworthy'. Third-party auditability is the top open problem; the reproduce link fails when published evals omit prompts, scoring rubrics, or model versions needed to re-run them.

**Direction:** Select a sample of publicly described safety evaluations from system cards and framework appendices and score each on reproducibility prerequisites: is the benchmark named, the prompt set available, the scoring rubric specified, the exact model version identified? Produce a reproducibility scorecard and flag which evals are unauditable in principle.

**Why it matters:** Auditable verification of safety claims is the central technical-governance problem. A concrete catalogue of which published evals can't even in principle be reproduced shows where disclosure standards must require artifacts. Document analysis, no compute, strongly counterfactual.

**Relevant context:** Open Problems in Technical AI Governance (third-party verification, audit consistency); arXiv:2411.13808 'GPAI Evaluations Standards Taskforce'; FLI AI Safety Index risk-assessment domain.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: third-party reproducibility of dangerous-capability evals is a pathway major safety orgs flag as critical for verification.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Scoring published evals against a reproducibility checklist; accessible to motivated beginners with no compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped scorecard exercise with well-defined presence/absence criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent verification work labs are disincentivized to do; public docs only.

novelty.reasoning: Eval-reproducibility is a recognized topic; this specific scorecard angle may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Reproducibility of published evals is discussed but a concrete cross-lab scorecard may be open.
